record.body: Biophony is the layer of sound produced by living organisms in an ecosystem: bird song at dawn, insect choruses at night, frog calls at a pond, whale song in the ocean, and the rustle and footfall of animals moving. Biophony varies by place, season, and time of day, and it carries ecological information: which species are present, whether they are breeding, and how healthy a habitat is. A rich biophony with many species calling in different frequency bands and time slots suggests a diverse community, while a silent habitat may signal disturbance, even when it looks intact. This record covers biophony alone, and it names the other layers only to keep them distinct: the wind behind the chorus is geophony, and any road noise is anthrophony.

demo.code:
TITLE = 'Biophony: The Living Layer'
BANDS = {'birds': 6, 'frogs': 4, 'insects': 10}
tot = float(sum(BANDS.values()))
print('Record: ' + TITLE)
print('Total: %d' % int(tot))
for k in sorted(BANDS):
    print('%s: %d (%.1f percent)' % (k, BANDS[k], 100.0 * BANDS[k] / tot))
demo.expected_output:
Record: Biophony: The Living Layer
Total: 20
birds: 6 (30.0 percent)
frogs: 4 (20.0 percent)
insects: 10 (50.0 percent)

record.math_proof: Math proof: if 6 bird species, 4 frog species, and 10 insect species call at a site, the calling community totals 6 + 4 + 10 = 20 species.
record.science_proof: Science proof: long-term soundscape recordings show that biophony tracks species presence and breeding activity, and that habitats with documented high biodiversity produce richer, more structured biophony than degraded habitats.
